cards.text: The Sadducees just took their shot at Jesus with a question about the resurrection, and He silenced them. So the Pharisees, another group of Jewish religious leaders, gather together. One crew walks off the field quiet, and the next crew is already stretching on the sideline like, “Put me in, coach!”

cards.question: One of the Pharisees steps up to test Jesus with a question. Who is he?

cards.text: This isn't a friendly chat. It's a test: “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?” Out of the WHOLE Law, pick ONE. No pressure!

cards.question: Out of the whole Law, which commandment does Jesus call the first and greatest?

cards.text: Jesus answers with a command from God's Law: “Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.” He calls it “the first and greatest commandment.”

cards.question: Heart, soul and mind. In the greatest commandment, Jesus is talking about loving God with ___ of you.

cards.text: The man asked for ONE commandment, and Jesus says there's a second one just like it. Friend, that's me when somebody asks for one cookie and walks out holding the whole box.

cards.question: Jesus says the second commandment is like the first one. What is it?

answers.text: Give to your neighbor in need

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says these two commandments, loving God and loving your neighbor, are small next to the rest of the Law.

cards.text: Jesus says, “All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.” Picture that one hook by your front door holding every coat, every bag and every set of keys you own, and now picture somebody pulling it out of the wall. EVERYTHING hits the floor.
The Pharisees are still gathered, and now Jesus asks them: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?” The guys who came with the questions are now the ones in the hot seat.

cards.question: Jesus asks whose son the Christ is. The Pharisees answer that He is the son of ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus points them to something David, Israel's king, said in the Spirit. David says, “The Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.’”

cards.question: Jesus asked the Pharisees about the Christ, then quoted King David. In David's line, who is the one David calls “my Lord”?
Jesus asks the Pharisees, “So if David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how can He be David’s son?” What makes that so hard to answer?

answers.text: David would be calling his own son Lord
David would be calling an enemy his Lord
David would be calling a stranger his Lord

cards.text: Think about it, friend. That's like your grandpa standing up when you walk in the room and calling you SIR, when Grandpa usually just wants to know why you never call.

cards.question: True or false: The Pharisees come right back at Jesus with a sharp answer to His question about David's Lord.
Nobody can answer Jesus a word. From that day on, what does no one dare to do?

cards.text: No one can answer a word, and from that day on, no one dares to question Him any further. It got so quiet you could hear the dust fall, and believe me, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer learning exactly what that sounds like.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "The Lord said to my Lord, 'Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.'", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says the Sadducees asked Jesus a question about the resurrection. That fact comes from outside the passage (Matthew 22:23-33), and the card gives no reference for it. The card cites only Matthew 22:34.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question says the man is "One of the Pharisees". That makes "A tax collector" easy to rule out, so the baker is down to two real options.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 5 quotes "with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind" right before card 6. Card 6 then asks the baker to fill in "all", which card 5 just showed three times.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke's actions don't match. In the text, Jesus answers with more than He was asked for: two commandments instead of one. In the joke, Papa Dorin greedily takes more than he asked for: the whole box instead of one cookie. Giving a fuller answer and grabbing extra are different actions, and the joke also turns one into the whole box.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The story card is only a joke. It tells no part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The punchline, "Grandpa usually just wants to know why you never call", is built on a stereotype about older relatives.

rule.text: Never puts down any person or group: no jokes about age, gender, race, nationality, accents, appearance, intelligence or church denomination.

findings.problem: Card 19 repeats what cards 17 and 18 already covered: no one could answer a word, and no one dared to question Him any further. It adds nothing new from the passage, so it works as a recap card.
